arxiv-2310-08583.title: Discovering Fatigued Movements for Virtual Character Animation 443 Journal: TOG Conference: SIGGRAPH Asia 2023 Conference Papers; December 12–15, 2023; Sydney, NSW, Australia SIGGRAPH Asia 2023 Conference Papers (SA Conference Papers ’23), December 12–15, 2023, Sydney, NSW, Australia DOI: 10.1145/36
arxiv-2310-08583.creator: Noshaba Cheema, Rui Xu, Nam Hee Kim, Perttu Hämäläinen, Vladislav Golyanik, Marc Habermann, Christian Theobalt, Philipp Slusallek
arxiv-2310-08583.description: Abstract . Virtual character animation and movement synthesis have advanced rapidly during recent years, especially through a combination of extensive motion capture datasets and machine learning. A remaining challenge is interactively simulating characters that fatigue when performing extended motions, which is indispensable for the realism of generated animations.

arxiv-2410-17636.title: Exoplanet Imaging Data Challenge, phase II: Comparison of algorithms in terms of characterization capabilities
arxiv-2410-17636.creator: Cantalloube F, Christiaens V, Cantero C, Cioppa A, Nasedkin E, Absil O, Delorme P, Wang J.-J, Bonse J. M, Daglayan H, Dahlqvist C.-H, Guyot N, Juillard S, Mazoyer J, Samland M, Sabalbal M, Ruffio J.-B, Van Droogenbroeck M
arxiv-2410-17636.description: Abstract In this communication, we report on the results of the second phase of the Exoplanet Imaging Data Challenge started in 2019. This second phase focuses on the characterization of point sources (exoplanet signals) within multispectral high-contrast images from ground-based telescopes.

arxiv-2412-12633.title: Arborescences of Random Covering Graphs
arxiv-2412-12633.creator: Muchen Ju, Junjie Ni, Kaixin Wang, Yihan Xiao
arxiv-2412-12633.description: Abstract . A rooted arborescence of a directed graph is a spanning tree directed towards a particular vertex. A recent work of Chepuri et al. [ 1 ] showed that the arborescences of a covering graph of a directed graph G G are closely related to the arborescences of G G .

arxiv-2503-20125.title: Hybrid FSO and RF Lunar Wireless Power Transfer
arxiv-2503-20125.creator: Barış Dönmez, Yanni Jiwan-Mercier, Sébastien Loranger, and Güneş Karabulut Kurt
arxiv-2503-20125.description: Abstract This study focuses on the feasibility analyses of the hybrid free-space optics (FSO) and radiofrequency (RF)-based wireless power transmission (WPT) system used in the realistic Cislunar environment, which is established by using system tool kit (STK) high-precision orbit propagator (HPOP) software in which many external forces are incorporated.

arxiv-2504-02760.title: Topological groupoids with involution and real algebraic stacks
arxiv-2504-02760.creator: Emiliano Ambrosi and Olivier de Gaay Fortman August 9, 2026
arxiv-2504-02760.description: Abstract To a topological groupoid endowed with an involution, we associate a topological groupoid of fixed points, generalizing the fixed-point subspace of a topological space with involution. We prove that when the topological groupoid with involution arises from a Deligne-Mumford stack over ℝ \mathbb{R} , this fixed locus coincides with the real locus of the stack.

pmc-11434394.title: Copper Serum Levels in the Hemodialysis Patient Population
pmc-11434394.creator: Guido Gembillo, Luigi Peritore, Vincenzo Labbozzetta, Alfio Edoardo Giuffrida, Antonella Lipari, Eugenia Spallino, Vincenzo Calabrese, Luca Visconti, Domenico Santoro, Giuseppe Lucarelli
pmc-11434394.description: Copper is an essential element in the diet of mammals, including humans. It plays an important role in the physiological regulation of various enzymes and is consequently involved in several biological processes such as angiogenesis, oxidative stress regulation, neuromodulation, and erythropoiesis.

pmc-11579912.title: Middle fossa approach for a petrous apex bony spur causing trigeminal neuralgia: illustrative case
pmc-11579912.creator: Forrest Hamrick, Samantha Colby, William T Couldwell, Shervin Rahimpour
pmc-11579912.description: BACKGROUNDTrigeminal neuralgia (TN) can arise from trigeminal nerve compression at the root entry zone due to neurovascular conflict, which most often presents in the 6th decade of life. The authors report the case of a young patient with TN with a petrous apex bony spur near the entrance of Meckel’s cave, causing compression of the proximal trigeminal nerve.

pmc-11894020.title: Occurrence of Trichinella spiralis in farmed wild boars (Sus scrofa): an underrated risk in China
pmc-11894020.creator: Nian-Zhang Zhang, Meng Wang, Wei-Gang Chen, Wen-Yan Gai, Thanh Thi Ha Dao, Ting-Ting Li, Wen-Hui Li, Hai-Rui Zhang, Hong Yin, Nguyen Thi Bich Thuy, Bao-Quan Fu
pmc-11894020.description: Keywords: Artificial digestion, multiplex PCR, Trichinella spiralis, wild boars Introduction Trichinellosis is a food-borne zoonotic parasitic disease caused by ingestion of Trichinella sp. infective larvae via consuming raw or undercooked meat (Pozio, 2015). The genus Trichinella consists of 13 taxa (10 species and 3 genotypes) distributed into 2 clades: encapsulated and nonencapsulated (Pozio, 2021).

pmc-12607186.title: Protocol for a multicenter, cluster-randomized, stepped-wedge, implementation trial of a prehospital sepsis protocol
pmc-12607186.creator: Shamie Das, Azeemuddin Ahmed, Olga Capurro, Michael J. Carr, Fabiana Barerro Castedo, Scott K. Fridkin, Alex Hall, Stacey House, Joseph Kellogg, Melissa Kroll, Nicholas Kurtzman, Rajashri Manjunath, C. Christina Mehta, Nicholas M. Mohr, Radhika Prakash-Asrani, Caroline C. Rudolph, Christine Spainhou
pmc-12607186.description: BackgroundSepsis is a common, life-threatening medical emergency in which early recognition and treatment are cornerstones of management. Best practice guidelines recommend standardized sepsis screening in hospitals to facilitate early recognition. In contrast, very little is known about the efficacy and safety of standardized sepsis screening in the prehospital Emergency Medical Services (EMS) environment.

pmc-12619079.title: Association Between Exposure to Smartphones and Tablets and Motor Development in Early Childhood: A Systematic Review
pmc-12619079.creator: Rinelly Pazinato Dutra, Yasmin Marques Castro, Veridiana Moran, Vicente Gabriel Wink Mattos, Paulo Victor Moura Rodrigues, Eliane Denise Araújo Bacil, Michael Pereira da Silva
pmc-12619079.description: BackgroundThis systematic review investigated the association between smartphone/tablet exposure and motor development in children aged 0–6 years.MethodsObservational studies in Portuguese, English or Spanish were included following the Participants, Exposure, Comparison, Outcomes and Study Design. A search conducted in November 2024 across seven databases identified 3228 records.

pmc-12654818.title: Magnified Dermoscopy in Skin Cancer and Infectious Skin Diseases
pmc-12654818.creator: Katarzyna Korecka, Joanna Pogorzelska-Dyrbuś, Adriana Polańska, Aleksandra Dańczak-Pazdrowska, Aimilios Lallas, Paola Savoia
pmc-12654818.description: Background and Objectives: Dermoscopy is a non-invasive clinical tool that allows for the in vivo visualization of pigmented and non-pigmented structures in the epidermis and the papillary dermis. The standard handheld dermoscopy offers a magnification of 10×, whereas the videodermatoscopes can obtain a magnification of up to 140×.

pmc-13102567.title: An inter-laboratory study of the multi-dimensional behaviors of analogue lumbar spine surrogates: towards standardization in spine testing
pmc-13102567.creator: Emma C. Coltoff, Siril Teja Dukkipati, Philip J. Brown, Mark Driscoll
pmc-13102567.description: IntroductionExperimental reproduction of lumbar spinal loading throughout activities of daily living is challenging and has historically relied on simplifications to the applied loading to pure moment testing along primary orthogonal anatomical planes. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the reproducibility and crossplatform translation of multi-dimensional spinal loading protocols between two distinct biomechanical testing systems.

pmc-13136898.title: Impact of alternative splicing on Arabidopsis proteome
pmc-13136898.creator: Andres V Reyes, Christopher Zhang, Sumudu S Karunadasa, Ruben Shrestha, TaraBryn S Grismer, Danbi Byun, Shou-Ling Xu
pmc-13136898.description: Limited proteomic evidence makes it unclear to what extent alternative splicing (AS) isoforms are translated and functionally relevant in eukaryotes. Here, we present a comprehensive proteomic analysis in plants using large-scale data mining, extensive fractionation of AspN- and trypsin-digested proteomes, and both label-free and TMT labeling.

pmc-13191978.title: Copeptin as a predictor of seizure diagnosis and seizure type in emergency department patients
pmc-13191978.creator: Ayça Çalbay, Murat Maksut Çalbay, Sultan Tuna Akgöl Gür, Fatma Şimşek, Nurinnisa Öztürk
pmc-13191978.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the diagnostic utility of serum copeptin (CPT) levels in distinguishing epileptic seizures from Pseudo or functional/dissociative seizures (FDS) in adult patients presenting to the emergency department, and to investigate possible differences in CPT levels among various seizure types.MethodsThis prospective, observational study was conducted at a tertiary research hospital between September 2023 and September 2024.

pmc-13247792.title: Methodological guidance on clinical prediction models in mental health research
pmc-13247792.creator: Raquel Costa, Bruno de Sousa, Thomas Kneib, Rui Martins, Andreas Mayr
pmc-13247792.description: Clinical prediction models play a crucial role in advancing personalized care for mental health disorders, providing essential insights for diagnosis, prognosis and intervention planning. This work examines the current methodological approaches used to develop such models, emphasizing their application to mental health problems, including depression.

pmc-13258330.title: Gastrointestinal Symptoms After Sport-Related Concussion: Prevalence and Patterns in a Multi-Cohort Analysis
pmc-13258330.creator: Emma Finnegan, Ed Daly, Katherine J. Hunzinger, Lisa Ryan
pmc-13258330.description: Background/Objectives: Concussions occur across all sports globally; however, inconsistent symptom recognition continues to challenge diagnosis, management, and recovery. Although concussion effects extend beyond neurological dysfunction, gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms remain insufficiently captured within current assessment frameworks and may influence athletes’ fuelling choices and food tolerance during recovery.
